content.text:
I've submitted index 1 (Ca 0.14, Fe 0.70, Mn 0.16) as the best composition. Its photocurrent was 1e-8 A, which is very low, and it was the only one of my three measurements with any signal, so the campaign likely scores poorly.

| Index | Ca / Fe / Mn | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.14 / 0.70 / 0.16 | 1e-8 |
| 74 | 0.50 / 0.35 / 0.16 | 0 |
| 4 | 0.22 / 0.66 / 0.12 | 0 |

- **How I chose:** I started with the most Fe-rich spot because the model results point to a hematite-like phase that absorbs the 2.4 eV light. For Fe₂O₃, the predicted band gap is 1.5 eV at the lower-accuracy setting and 2.8 eV at the higher one. The stability model puts Fe₂O₃ on the hull, meaning it is thermodynamically stable.
- **What the zeros suggest:** index 74 tested the Ca-rich side and gave nothing. Index 4 kept Fe high but had more Ca and less Mn, and also gave nothing, so adding Ca seems to hurt.
- **What I didn't do:** I didn't read the full phase list because the output was too large. I also used none of the 5 XRD measurements, so no crystal phase was confirmed.
- **Unexplored areas:** the Mn-rich region (above about 0.4 Mn) and the middle of the composition range were never measured, so a better composition may be there.
